events.title: Playfight XBerg
events.location: Capoeira Akademie Berlin, Hasenheide 9 (im 2. Hinterhof 1.Stock), 10967 Berlin
events.description: Spielerisch kämpfen balgen wie als Kind unbeschwert herumkugeln raufen wie die Tierkinder ausgelassen toben Unter Anleitung und mit festen Regeln. Jeden 2. und 4. Samstag im Monat von 20-23:00h (Einlass ab 16:45) 15€ an der Abendkasse, mit Reservierung per E-Mail 10€, info@playfight-xberg.de , www.playfight-xberg.de Aktuelles: Einladungslink zu unserem Telegram-Kanal für Termine, Neuigkeiten, und Änderungen (falls es mal welche gibt): https://t.me/+lNpr9L9e-mc5Nzky Und worum geht’s im playfight xberg? Playfight bringt kreative Ideen und ausgelassenes Spielen mit achtsamem Kämpfen in einer sicheren und respektvollen Umgebung zusammen. Wir kämpfen miteinander und nicht gegeneinander. Es geht uns ums Spaß haben und nicht ums besiegen. Wir setzen unsere Kräfte ein ohne verletzen zu wollen. Vorsichtig, spielerisch, kräftiger, ausgelassen, achtsam. Bei uns wird viel gelacht. Playfight macht Spaß – und manchmal sogar ein deutliches Glücksgefühl. Vorerfahrung im Kämpfen oder besondere sportliche Fitness ist nicht erforderlich. Faire MitspielerInnen sind uns herzlich willkommen. Wir nehmen aufeinander Rücksicht und begegnen einander mit Respekt und Neugierde. Es geht uns um Körperkontakt ohne sexuellen Kontext, um Bewegung und darum intensiven Spaß zu haben. Regeln Wir playfighten maximal in Kniehöhe, um die Fallhöhe gering zu halten Jede/r kann jederzeit STOP sagen oder 3 mal abklopfen. Die Situation wird damit sofort beendet. Das bedeutet nicht unbedingt, dass der Kampf ganz abgebrochen werden muss, sondern man kann auch kurz stoppen und die Lage klären. Ausdrücklich verboten sind Kampftechniken, deren Zweck es ist, zu verletzen, also KEIN Würgen, Treten, Schlagen, Hebeln, Beißen, festes Haare ziehen… Vor einem Kampf können Vorabspachen über spezielle Wünsche oder/und persönliche Empfindlichkeiten getroffen werden. Ihr könnt aber auch einfach schauen, welche Dynamik sich zwischen euch entwickelt, man kann sich auch während des Spielens weiter absprechen, und ansonsten kann man im Zweifelsfall ja jederzeit einfach „STOP“ sagen und die Situation klären. Ablauf Aufwärmen und Kurzworkshop • wir aktivieren unseren unseren Körper mit verschiedenen Übungen • üben praktisch ein, die eigenen Grenzen zu setzen und die des Grenzen des Partners zu respektieren • probieren verschiedene Ideen aus wie man kämpfen kann • machen ein kleine Roll- und Fallschule • und lernen uns dabei natürlich schon ein bisschen kennen Hauptteil Zum Kämpfen treffen sich 2 Personen in der Mitte des Kreises. KampfpartnerInnen können sich auf verschiedene Art finden. Wer aufgefordert wird und nicht möchte, sagt oder signalisiert einfach „Nein“, ohne dass das nein begründet werden muss. Die anderen TeilnehmerInnen bilden den Außenkreis und beobachten den Kampf und helfen dadurch einen sicheren Raum zu schaffen. Bitte beachten: • Schmuck bitte ablegen oder abkleben • du solltest unbedingt etwas zu trinken (oder eine leere Flasche für Leitungswasser) mitbringen. • unsere Bodenmatten sind in Hinsicht Hautabschürfungen ziemlich harmlos, aber um ganz sicher zu sein dass du sie vermeidest, bring am besten langärmlige und -beinige Kleidung und Socken mit. Vorerfahrung oder besondere sportliche Fitness ist nicht erforderlich. Außerdem gilt noch: Playfight ist Sport. Blaue Flecken und Abschürfungen sind beim playfight normal. Größere Verletzungen kommen extrem selten vor. Wir übernehmen keine Haftung, jede/r nimmt auf eigene Verantwortung teil. Infos zu den Räumlichkeiten und zum Host Ulf findet ihr auf der homepage. We are a safe space for LGBTQ+ and everyone else.

events.title: Feu Marinho
events.description:
Feu Marinho is a Brazilian singer, songwriter, and composer whose music blends Brazilian traditions, jazz, and oriental influences, shaped by themes of memory, movement, and human experience.

Joined by Malte Bogner, Yonatan Harari, César Belleyguier, Yannick Mäetelle and Nir Kleiner Feu is preparing to release his second album, Volume, in 2027. Co-produced by Feu,  Bogner, and Harari, the record expands his sound through rich arrangements and a collaborative creative process.

Having performed and toured across Europe, Asia, and Africa, Feu has developed an international presence through collaborations with artists from diverse musical backgrounds, including Jacob Collier, Daniel Harlev, Itay Spiegel, and Panda do Sol.

With Volume, Feu continues to explore the meeting point between cultures, composition, and improvisation, creating performances that move between intimacy and openness, shaped by the sounds and encounters that inspire his journey.

events.title: Will Jacobs & The Unit – BERLIN LATE ALBUM RELEASE CONCERT – "GOLDFISH BLUES"
events.description: Will Jacobs & The Unit BERLIN LATE ALBUM RELEASE CONCERT „ GOLDFISH BLUES “ WITH : Christian Keymer-Arne Imig-Brian D. Sauls Deutsch Mit dem Treffen auf Arne Imig , Christian Keymer und Brian D. Sauls fand Will Jacobs 2023 seine neue musikalische Heimat, die unter dem Namen „Will Jacobs & The Unit“ den Soul-, Blues- und Funk-Sound der 60er Jahre mit Elementen aus Neo-Soul und modernem R&B neu interpretiert. Die dadurch geschlagene Brücke zwischen den Generationen begeistert seit jeher das Publikum vieler renommierter Jazz-Clubs und Festivals in ganz Europa. Will Jacobs verbrachte seine Jugend damit, in den Blues Clubs Chicagos von den wahren Größen des Genres zu lernen und entwickelte so einen Sound, der heutzutage nur noch selten aufzufinden ist. Durch diesen authentischen, energievollen Sound gewann er den Jugendpreis bei der Windy City Blues Challenge in Chicago und bekam kurz darauf die Chance, beim internationalen Blues Showcase in Memphis, Tennessee aufzutreten. Diese Erfolge führten ihn direkt ans renommierte Berklee College of Music, wo er sich weiteren Genres widmete. Nach mehreren Tourneen mit dem berühmten Zydeco Künstler, C.J. Chenier, einer erfolgreichen Karriere in der Blues Szene Chicagos und einem längeren musikalischen Aufenthalt in Sri Lanka wagte er 2016 den Sprung nach Europa, um von Berlin aus als Solokünstler durchzustarten. Daraufhin folgte eine Orientierungsphase in der deutschen Blues-Landschaft, zahlreichen Konzerten, unterschiedlichen Besetzungen (Blues Caravan, Marcos Coll Band, David Haynes & Friends) und der Veröffentlichung eines ersten Solo-Albums „Goldfish Blues“ bei Ruf Records. English In 2023 Will Jacobs found his new musical home after meeting Arne Imig (bass), Christian Keymer (keys), and Brian D. Sauls (drums). Under the name „Will Jacobs & The Unit“ they offer a fresh perspective on the soul, blues, and funk sounds of the 60s by merging them with elements of neo-soul and modern R&B. They manage to seamlessly bridge the gap between generations and have consistently delighted the audiences of many renowned jazz clubs and festivals throughout Europe. Will Jacobs spent his youth immersing himself in Chicago’s blues clubs, learning from the true greats of the genre. This foundation cultivated a rare, profound sound, which allowed him to attract local and international attention with his first band, performing at the International Blues Showcase in Memphis, Tennessee after having won Chicago’s Windy City Blues Challenge (Youth Division). These successes propelled him to the esteemed Berklee College of Music, where his focus broadened to embrace more contemporary genres. After a few successful years of gigging, composing and session work in Chicago, a musical residency in Sri Lanka, as well as touring with renowned Zydeco artist C.J. Chenier, Will embarked on his solo career, relocating to Berlin, Germany in 2016. What followed was a period of orientation in the European blues scene, numerous concerts with various lineups (Blues Caravan, Marcos Coll Band, David Haynes & Friends), and the release of his first solo album, „Goldfish Blues,“ on Ruf Records. Will Jacobs – Guitar & Vocals Christian Keymer – Keyboards & Backing Vocal Arne Imig – Bass Brian D. Sauls – Drums & Backing Vocal

events.title: CAROLINA BUBBICO – «Vocàlia» – GroundUp Records New Album Tour
events.description: CAROLINA BUBBICO « Vocàlia » GroundUp Records New Album Tour FEAT : Filippo Bubbico-Gabriel Prado The Vocàlia Live Tour presents the fourth album by Carolina Bubbico , to be released on April 10, 2026 on the US label GroundUp Music, preceded by two singles “ Everlove ” and “ Uma Rosa e Um Bordado ”. Vocàlia is a love letter to life and a message of hope dedicated to future generations . Conceived as a multilingual vocal orchestra, the project is rooted in a deeply transformative period of the artist’s life, motherhood, experienced as a moment of rebirth, change, and renewed creative clarity. Inspired by the Latin word for vowels, the project imagines a poetic world where the voice becomes an expansive vehicle for ancestry, femininity, and collective expression. The title Vocàlia draws from Latin origins and refers to vowels, the fundamental elements of language and singing . Here, the voice becomes the absolute protagonist: feminine, collective, ancestral. After fifteen years of research into vocal polyphony, through loop-based performance and choral ensembles, Bubbico takes on the challenge of creating music arranged exclusively for voices, shaping a cohesive and contemporary sound. Vocàlia unfolds as a living vocal organism: voices create call-and-response patterns, harmonic textures, and rhythmic structures, at times evoking brass sections, string ensembles, or percussive layers. The creative process flows as a musical stream of consciousness, symbolically represented by a crocheted doily, each thread, like each voice, interwoven into a complex yet balanced structure. The album features lyrics in multiple languages, written in collaboration with Becca Stevens, Greta Panettieri, Giuseppe Anastasi, Simona Severini, Lauryyn, Antonio Villeroy, and Cristiana Verardo, exploring themes of rebirth, resilience, simplicity, and love for life. Two special guests appear on the record: Becca Stevens on Everlove and Mari Jasca on Uma rosa e um bordado. Rhythmic elements were recorded by Finnish percussionist Abdissa Assefa, whose work draws from diverse global musical traditions. The album is produced by Filippo Bubbico, who also performed and processed the synth bass parts, contributing to the project’s contemporary and exploratory sound. Carolina Bubbico – Vocals, Percussions Filippo Bubbico – Bass, Vocals Gabriel Prado – Percussions, Vocals Fotos Carolina©Sunvillage Records

Here’s what Richard Williams wrote about me in his blog: « If you’re ever at a loose end in Berlin on a Monday night, my advice would be to head for A-Trane, the jazz club in Charlottenburg, where Andreas Schmidt, a pianist, composer and teacher at the city’s Jazz Institut, holds a weekly free-admission session featuring a changing cast. Schmidt is a fine pianist, the salient features of his playing located somewhere between the Paul Bley of the mid-’60s and the Chick Corea of «Now He Sings, Now He Sobs». You might get an idea of his approach if I say that his first album was made (in 1995) with Lee Konitz, and a later one comprised a duo with Gary Peacock. /////// TWO-SONG TUESDAY ///////
[sign up 19:30 // start 20:00]
CALLING ALL SONGWRITERS, COMPOSERS, INSTRUMENTALISTS, POETS, WRITERS, STORYTELLERS, SYNTH WIZARDS, BAGPIPE SAVANTS, BROKEN HEARTS, TAP DANCERS, POLE DANCERS, MIND MELDERS, RACE CAR DRIVERS, AND AGNOSTIC SAINTS!

Set 2: 21:15

"The Same Procedure as Every Week, James."
- The random-order setlists appear at 19:45 at http://donau115.de
- First come, first booked, randomly-assigned slot, 15 slots per night + an overflow maybe list that we rarely get to.
- The bar staff tell you how to sign up, starting at 7.30pm. It is usually a link to an online sign-up form.
- Your set may include TWO SONGS or last TEN MINUTES, WHICHEVER IS SHORTER (e.g. two seven-minute songs = NO, three three-minute songs = NO).
- NO SOUNDCHECKS. Be ready. Slip on, blow minds, slip off. Setup is 90 seconds.
- Sets are no longer than 10 minutes. THERE IS A STOPWATCH TO ENSURE THIS. If your set goes beyond 10 minutes, the stopwatch goes off in the middle of your song. (The alarm sound is in the key of C#, FYI, so modulate to that key for a smooth overtime ending.)
- For the love of God, DO NOT PLAY THE SAME SONG OVER AND OVER EVERY WEEK. THIS IS BORING. TRY NEW THINGS. WE ADORE YOU. TAKE RISKS! ❤ ❤ ❤
- Out of respect for our neighbours:
--- you may NOT use loud percussion or send loud bass-heavy signals into the PA.
--- you may NOT bring your own amp
--- you are welcome to use the following itwms from our backline: piano, two generic vocal microphones, and a guitar cable directly into our PA.
--- DON'T COUNT ON US HAVING ANYTHING OTHER THAN THE FEW THINGS LISTED ABOVE. COME PREPARED.

events.title: Rope for Nerds: Detail Focus & Debugging
events.description:
Welcome back to Rope for Nerds — the workshop series for rope brains who want to really understand what’s going on under the hood. 
This session is all about refinement: the often-overlooked micro-skills and subtle mechanics that elevate your rope from “functional” to “flawlessly intentional.” Whether you’re chasing the mythical perfect single-column tie or endlessly fiddling with your tension to no avail, this workshop compiles years of niche knowledge into a concentrated toolkit you didn’t know you needed. 
We’ll break down the biomechanics of tying

How to control tension consistently
How rope behaves under load and movement
What actually makes a single-column tie “good,” and how to identify weak links
How to increase flow and make movement easy

And then—debugging
Because let’s be honest: ties don’t always go as planned. Ceci will introduce a practical Rope Debugging Checklist — a system for analyzing and troubleshooting your rope in real time. Bring your toughest knots, recurring frustrations, and messy half-solutions. You’ll get hands-on help in problem-solving real-world issues, and leave with better strategies for working through technical glitches on your own. 
Expect lots of tinkering, a healthy dose of analysis, and plenty of “ah-ha!” moments. Rope as craft. Rope as puzzle. Rope as precision instrument. Let’s get into it. 
Ideal For

Technically-minded riggers, bottoms, and switches
The nerdiest of the nerds
Beginners, the people who think they already know it all, and the people who got over that phase and know they still have years to learn
Anyone who loves diagrams, efficiency, or the phrase “root cause analysis”

events.title: Florian Zimmer
events.description:
Florian Zimmer has been in a creative dialogue with artists in a variety of bands and duos in the course of the past three decades, including the long-running avant-hop trio Saroos alongside Christoph Brandner and Max Punktezahl, the industrial-punk project TVII SON, the dubwise duo Driftmachine featuring Andreas Gerth, and most recently his project Bella Wakame with prolific percussionist Andreas Haberl. Now the Berlin-based musician and composer is about to get even busier, this time as a solo artist. His improvised live sets draw on dub techniques and subtle grooves, mixing the sounds of his trusted modular synthesizers with a wide variety of samples to lysergic effect.

Zimmer straddles the line between abstract sound collaging and spontaneous live composition, utilising sounds from exotica or old educational records as well as field recordings to create ambiguities. Whether it is layered-and-looped polylogues between disembodied voices punctuated by melancholic melodica sounds, minimalist electronica, or intricate modular synthesizer rhythms that wouldn’t feel out of place on the dancefloor: Zimmer’s genre-transcending work with and around contrasts creates a sense of familiarity while evoking a feeling of uncanniness. The ever-changing interplay between sounds and rhythms, abstraction and concretion, semiotic serendipity and emotional warmth forms the dynamic and atmospheric core of his solo work.

events.title: Midori Hirano
events.description:
Midori Hirano is a Berlin-based Japanese musician, composer, and sound artist originally from Kyoto. Rooted in classical piano, she explores the space between structure and abstraction, acoustic and electronic sound. Her music builds layered soundscapes from piano, synthesizers, field recordings, and processed electronics, bringing the harmonic thinking of her piano background into experimental sound.

She has worked with a diverse range of artists, including string player Atsuko Hatano on Water Ladder (2021, Alien Transistor), Hprizm of Anti Pop Consortium (Love Control, 2017, raster), Brueder Selke on Split Scale (2025, Thrill Jockey), CoH on Sudden Fruit (2025, Ici d'ailleurs) and Ilpo Väisänen of Pan Sonic, with whom she has performed live. 

Her new solo album OTONOMA (February 2026) has been released on Thrill Jockey Records, followed by The Juniper Tree (October 2026), an album featuring her newly imagined score for Nietzchka Keene’s 1990 film of the same name, following its live premiere at Videodroom in Ghent in 2025. The album was released by VIERNULVIER Records, with the digital edition on Thrill Jockey Records.

events.title: Care Planning

It’s December, and silly season is in full swing. With the demands, expectations, celebrations, and emotional intensity that can come with this time of year, how can you prepare for what lies ahead while still making space for joy and pleasure? 
Caritia invites participants to create care plans that support the whole self—not just through the busy Christmas season, but beyond it. Together, we’ll explore how to intentionally build beauty, rest, connection, pleasure, and support into our days, wherever we are in the world. 
This is a collaborative space for checking in with yourself, identifying what you need, and making practical and imaginative plans to help you move through the season with greater care and intention. 
What we’ll explore

Where am I now? — Exploring our current location, circumstances, capacity, and needs
Tuning in — Listening to the signals of the mind, body, and nervous system
Aligning with intention — Identifying what we want to cultivate, protect, and prioritise
Releases for every part — Exploring physical and psychological ways to let go of tension and accumulated stress
Emotional expression space — Making room for feelings that may need acknowledgement, expression, or movement
Planning for dissociation — Considering what support, grounding, and aftercare might be useful when we need to disconnect or retreat

Come as you are, and leave with a care plan that is uniquely yours.

events.title: Igor Osypov "Flying House"
events.description:
Igor Osypov presents his recent and most open-hearted project. Flying House opens a musical world with the unmistakable voice of guitarist Igor Osypov. The band presents a highly individual and immediately recognisable sound, balancing lyrical delicacy with dynamic rhythmic energy. The quartet’s subtle interplay and expressive depth create a sonic identity that is both distinctive and deeply memorable, leaving a lasting impression on the listener.

Flying House is a deeply personal upcoming album by guitarist Igor Osypov. In this music, Osypov dedicates each piece to the people and moments that shape his life—especially his family. The album focuses intentionally on the positive: cherishing the present, appreciating closeness, and finding warmth in the everyday.

Having spent much of his life as a refugee, escaping the reality of war, Osypov chose to center this project around a simple idea: living in the present. Flying House represents the feeling that home is not a fixed place but something that travels with the people you love. Wherever life takes you, home exists when those closest to you are near.

As a composer, Osypov returned to his most natural starting point: writing the music on his main instrument, the guitar. In this sense, the guitar becomes a metaphor for returning to one’s default setting, one’s musical home. While the guitar holds a central role in the sound of the album, the music leaves ample space for every member of the band to breathe, interact, and contribute their voice to the collective story.

Flying House is ultimately a celebration of presence, family, and the quiet joy of sharing music—and life—with the people who make any place feel like home.

events.description:
It’s the kinkiest time of the year—or at least it could be 😉 
December, Christmas, and all the expectations that surround them can bring up a surprisingly complicated mix of feelings. What if, instead of simply getting through the season, we played with it? How might our existing kinks, desires, and pleasures help us create new associations with this time of year? 
Caritia invites participants into a playful workshop exploring how kink can become a tool for connection, creativity, and pleasure during the festive season. We’ll imagine possibilities for play that feel nourishing, exciting, mischievous, or simply different from the usual Christmas script. 
This is a space to explore what makes play meaningful for you and to develop ideas, rituals, and possibilities that you can carry into the season and beyond. 
What we’ll explore

Christmas, but make it kinky — Reimagining familiar festive themes through a kink lens
Pleasure and possibility — Identifying the kinds of play, sensation, connection, and dynamics that appeal to us
Changing the associations — Exploring how intentional play can help us relate differently to challenging or loaded experiences
Play planning — Turning ideas and fantasies into realistic possibilities for connection and experimentation
Kink as care — Considering how play can support regulation, connection, confidence, and joy

Bring your curiosity, your festive mischief, and your favourite ways of playing. Let’s make some new Christmas traditions.

events.title: SMishmas
events.description:
Do you hate Christmas? Perhaps you just haven’t found the right way to celebrate it. 
SMishmas invites you to embrace the darker, stranger, more deliciously mischievous side of the festive season. Caritia welcomes participants into a playful exploration of sadism, masochism, sensation, and psychological play, using the imagery and absurdity of Christmas as our creative playground. 
December can be a season of slowing down, hibernating, and releasing. What kinds of kink might help us surrender, discharge tension, explore intensity, or regulate our nervous systems? What happens when we take the familiar symbols of Christmas and turn them into opportunities for sensation, transformation, catharsis, and play? 
Think shiny baubles, human Christmas trees, tinkling lights, starry patterns, festive cruelty, and a healthy dose of Scrooge-inspired attitude. 
This is a collaborative space for creating and exploring scenes together, with room for participants to bring their own ideas and interests. Come ready to be creatively mean, wonderfully strange, and playful with the season. 
What will happen in the space?

Intros & arrival — Getting settled, connecting, and establishing the foundations for the space
Brainstorming — Generating festive, kinky, and creatively cruel possibilities
Collaborative scene curation — Shaping ideas into shared scenes with clear intentions and boundaries
Playtime — Exploring sensation, dynamics, and Christmas-themed SM together
Wind-down & reflection — Returning to ourselves and considering: What gifts are you taking away with you?

Let’s be mean together. After all, it’s Christmas.

events.title: Digital Independence Day
events.description:
Eventpate: uhuspecht

Am ersten Sonntag kdes Monats auf die gute Seite wechseln!

Wir unterstützen dich dabei, deine digitale Autonomie zurückzugewinnen. Gemeinsam und Schritt für Schritt. Ob von X zu Mastodon, von Google Chrome zu Firefox – wir helfen dir beim Wechsel!

Warum nicht einen Email-Dienst mit mehr Privatsphäre probieren? Oder magst du bei einem Kaffee einfach mehr über andere digitale Alternativen erfahren, die unsere Demokratie stärken statt sie zu zerstören? Alternativen, die uns allen eine nachhaltige und selbstbestimmte Teilhabe sichern?

Dann lass uns zusammen loslegen!

Es gibt Tee, Kaffee, Snacks und natürlich Cookies. Lasst uns etwas für unsere digitale Unabhängigkeit tun! Kostenlos, auch ohne Vorkenntnisse. Bring aber gern deine Endgeräte mit.

Der Zugang und der Raum sind barrierefrei.

Wieder mit dabei sind als Gastgeber der Hackspace c-base, das Projekt Digital-Zebra (VÖBB), Topio, der kleindatenverein, Anoxinon e.V., Computertruhe e.V. und der Möckernkiez e.V. .

*Gemeinsam mehr erreichen*

Diese Veranstaltung ist Teil eines Netzwerks aus mehreren Organisationen und Initiativen in Berlin. Wir unterstützen uns gegenseitig mit Kompetenz, Erfahrung und praktischer Hilfe. Uns alle eint der Wunsch, Wissen zu teilen, voneinander zu lernen und solidarisch zusammenzuarbeiten.

Der DIDay bildet dabei den gemeinsamen Rahmen, in dem wir uns für digitale Selbstbestimmung und nachhaltige digitale Strukturen einsetzen.

Schau deshalb gern auch bei den Veranstaltungen der anderen beteiligten Organisationen vorbei. So entsteht ein vielfältiges Angebot, das Austausch, Vernetzung und gegenseitige Unterstützung lebendig macht.

events.title: BIPOC Utopias - Celebration
events.description:
This is a monthly separatist space to discuss and lab about kink, intimacy, and virtual play space for black, brown and Indigenous folks. 
For quite some time, Caritia has been musing on how to encourage and inspire more BIPOC into the realm of alternative lifestyles and ways of relating. There are many systemic barriers to this, including patriarchy, capitalism, classism and racism. In an effort to change the narrative, Caritia wishes to offer a monthly gathering for BIPOC to talk, learn about a topic or practice, and support one another through a community actively built together, with the aspiration to gather in person once a year. 
Caritia’s intention is to create a guided, active space for learning and coming together. This format has the potential to morph and change as the group sees fit. 
This month’s topic
Celebration: Let’s celebrate our diversity, desires and ways we wish to manifest the changes we want to see in the world.

events.title: Kink is Political - Restraint
events.description:
In this session, we’ll read bondage and restraint as sexual practices within the context of BDSM against a broader history of restraint. Turning towards the anti-psychiatric work of Franco Basaglia and the ubiquity of physical restraint as a tool of the medical establishment and carceral state, we’ll start to contend with what it means to take up and play with forms and techniques implicated in an almost unimaginable amount of violence and harm. We’ll ask: what logics of restraint in medical and carceral contexts end up reproduced in kink and sex-positive communities? How does the broader social and political practice of restraint shape who our spaces are accessible to and how? What are the impacts of legislation that criminalizes voluntary restraint? How do we take restraint more seriously?  
About this series
Kink is Political is an online discussion with Addie Tahl, Georg Barkas, Andrea Rimon, and occasional special guests. Participants are invited to join a discussion during which we unite critique with an emphasis on the practical and day-to-day issues and challenges of kink, intimacy, and relationships. 
Focusing on concepts central to BDSM, leather, rope, and sex-positive communities, it interrogates widely adopted approaches and commonly held notions. It aims to understand the politics of kink beyond the language of sexual liberation and politics of sexual liberalism, both frames that have proven insufficient in addressing widespread harm, a rising international tide of sex-negativity and reaction, or in guaranteeing that the most marginalized can sexually flourish. 
Kink is Political is an examination of the contexts and consequences of how we talk about and understand gender and sexuality. It is a forum to think about how kink spaces and practices operate, what works, what doesn’t, and what we can use to build something better.

events.title: Rope Hangout: Decorations
events.description:
A rope hangout is a welcoming, peer-to-peer space where we research rope together, connect, and explore in a relaxed, pressure-free atmosphere, no matter your experience level. All forms of rope bondage (Japanese inspired shibari/kinbaku, western style bondage, decorative macrame…) are warmly invited. 
Whether you feel like tying or simply being present, you’re welcome here. Enjoy non-alcoholic drinks, snacks, and easy conversation — sometimes just showing up is enough. There’s no pressure to perform, teach, or know anything in advance. Curiosity and your (imaginary) lab coat is all you need to bring. 
This month’s special focus: Decorations
The festive season is upon us. Let’s take this opportunity to focus on decorations: how to make the ropes pretty, clean up our suspension lines, do some erotic macrame, or use rope to wrap gifts. Maximalist or minimalist, we’re labbing out on aesthetics. 
The theme is an open invitation rather than a guideline. You’re always encouraged to follow your own interests, bring questions, share experiences, or simply observe and take it all in. The space is shaped by what each person brings into it. 
Note: This is not a rope jam/play space. Rope Hangout is a peer learning environment.

Für Wen?

Endo cis persons are also welcome to attend, regardless of whether or not they are specific (play) partners or friends of TIN persons. It is only important to us that they understand the nature of the space they are entering and respect it. This is not a party for endo-cis-hetero couples to play at. 
What?
TIN + Friends is a play party without a focus on specific fetishes, kinks, or BDSM practices. Apart from the focus described above, the party/play culture is similar to that of other queer parties at Quälgeist. Feel free to use our versatile play area, whether you come with a planned playdate or have just met at the bar. 
At 7:00 p.m. there is an introduction round that you are welcome to participate in. This is especially recommended for persons who are still new to the community or want to meet new people.
After the introduction round, we usually offer a ´Special´ to make it even easier to get in touch with each other. You can find out what we have planned for the next party on our Instagram account. 
When?
The party always takes place on the second Thursday of the month, 6 p.m. – 11 p.m., introduction round  start at 7 p.m. 
If you have any questions about the party, would like to give us feedback, or want to contact the TIN + Friends team for any other reason, you can reach us by email at: tin@quaelgeist.sm

events.title: Breath Play with Ropes
events.description:
During a bondage session, the breathing of the tied person is often impacted. Even a simple chest harness can become real torture when breathing in certain positions. Rope is a perfect tool for exploring breath play. A rigger can influence their partner’s breathing through different areas: the mouth, throat, ribcage, or abdomen. 
Before experimenting, we’ll take time to understand how breathing works, what happens in the body during breath restriction, and how to recognize and reduce the risks involved. We’ll also discuss how to communicate clearly with your partner before, during, and after this type of play, so that everyone can make informed decisions and stay within their own boundaries. 
This workshop is also deeply focused on the experience of the tied person. We’ll explore the wide range of physical sensations, emotional responses, and psychological states that breath play can evoke, and learn how to observe, understand, and respond to them
throughout a rope scene. 
Once we’ve covered these foundations, we’ll experiment with different ways of incorporating breath play into rope. Breath play can be a powerful way to communicate through ropes, creating an intimate dialogue built on trust, attention, and mutual awareness.

events.title: Boundaries and Negotiations - Holiday Edition
events.description:
The holiday season can be a particularly interesting time to think about boundaries. December often brings increased social expectations and obligations—all of which can stretch, blur, or challenge the boundaries we usually rely on. 
Boundaries can feel like a slippery concept: something we’re constantly told to uphold, understand, and recognise when crossed. Yet many of us have never had the opportunity to explore what a boundary actually means to us, where our boundaries come from, or how they have been shaped by our experiences. 
How did you come to understand boundaries in your life? What have your culture, family, community, relationships, laws, and personal experiences taught you about saying yes, saying no, asking for what you need, and responding when someone else says no? 
Caritia invites participants into a practical and reflective space to explore boundaries and negotiation through a holiday-season lens. Together, we’ll look at the difference between boundaries, preferences, needs, limits, and agreements, and how we can communicate them with greater clarity and confidence. 
Rather than treating boundaries as fixed rules, we’ll explore them as something we can notice, communicate, negotiate, and revisit as our circumstances and capacity change. 
What we will offer

Exploring our boundary stories — Reflecting on how we learned what boundaries are and what has shaped our understanding of them
Boundaries, limits & preferences — Unpacking the differences and why they matter when we negotiate
The holiday pressure cooker — Exploring festive situations where boundaries can become complicated or harder to communicate
Negotiation in practice — Finding language for making requests, expressing limits, checking in, and responding to changing needs
Capacity & context — Considering how energy, stress, relationships, and social expectations affect what we are able and willing to do
When boundaries change — Practising how to communicate when our capacity, desires, or boundaries shift
Repair & renegotiation — Exploring what we can do when communication goes wrong, expectations change, or a boundary is crossed
Creating our own festive toolkit — Leaving with practical ideas and language to support clearer, more intentional negotiations throughout the season

An opportunity to move beyond the idea that boundaries are simply about saying no, and explore how they can help us create more satisfying, respectful, connected, and consensual experiences.

events.description:
Welcome to the Singles Rope Jam, a space for you to find new rope friends and tying partners (or rekindle old ropelationships). Ceci will guide you through a collective warm up, starting with a moment of grounding self-tying and then finding a partner or a small group to tie with. Afterwards you will have plenty of time to chat, tie, and connect in our lovely big house. The garden with suspension points and hashiras will also be open for you if it’s not raining. 
What happens at the Singles Rope Jam?

Space introduction and intro round at 7.30pm
Guided self-tying and tying in pairs or small groups
Free mingling, cruising space, and tying with people

All participation is voluntary, and you get to choose who you want to partner with, or stay with self-tying for part or all of the event. Ceci is available for any support you might need around navigating the social space. Doors open at 7pm and close at 9pm. We play the gongs 30 minutes before closing so you can finish calmly and don’t need to rush. 
Who is the Singles Rope Jam for?

Anyone who is curious about tying with new people
Adventurers who want to have a new experience
Socially anxious people who need some guidance to get warmed up

This is a sober space for people under the LGBTQIA+ umbrella, we embrace all experience levels and identities within this spectrum. We welcome all roles: people tying, people getting tied, switches, self tyers, rope sluts, nerds, and everyone in between.

events.title: Reimagining Connection: What is Relationship Anarchy?
events.description:
What if relationships didn’t have to follow a script? 
Relationship anarchy invites us to question the norms we’ve inherited about love, intimacy, commitment, and hierarchy. Instead of placing relationships into predefined categories, it asks: what feels true, consensual, and meaningful for you? 
This discussion-based workshop offers a welcoming space to explore these ideas together. Through guided conversation and reflection, Caritia supports participants in unpacking assumptions, sharing perspectives, and imagining new ways of relating—grounded in autonomy, honesty, and care. 
Whether you’re deeply familiar with relationship anarchy or simply curious, you’re invited to join a collective inquiry into what connection can look like when we let go of rigid expectations. 
What we’ll explore together:

The core principles of relationship anarchy and how they differ from traditional relationship models
How social norms and conditioning shape our expectations around love, sex, and commitment
Navigating autonomy, boundaries, and responsibility in non-hierarchical relationships
Communication practices that support clarity, and mutual respect
The challenges and possibilities of building relationships without predefined rules

Note: 
This is a discussion-based workshop with optional sharing. All experiences and perspectives are welcome. No prior knowledge is needed—just curiosity and respect for others.

Holding, hugs, and/or other types of comfortable touch
Guided conversations that deepen understanding and empathy
Playful moments that invite laughter and ease

Take-home practices you can use long after the workshop ends

events.description: A-TRANE PRÄSENTIERT: ANDREAS SCHMIDT& FRIENDS HEUTE MIT: EINTRITT FREI & ENTRANCE FREE Auf dem unteren Link zur Facebookseite von Andreas Schmidt erfahren Sie, wer alles an diesem Konzerttag auftreten wird. Um die Spontanität zu erhalten, was die Montagskonzerte von Andreas Schmidt & Friends ausmacht, werden die Musiker kurzfristig bekannt gegeben, Facebook Andreas Schmidt It´s me, the Monday A-Trane pianist Andreas Schmidt . Since 1995 I played here about 900 wonderful & surprising improvised happenings in music with lots of friends like Jay Clayton, Hayden Chisholm, Dave Douglas, Walter Norris, Mark Murphy, Till Brönner, Sebastian Merk, Andreas Edelmann, Jan Roder, Connie Crothers, Max Andrzejewski, Andy Fite etc.. Here’s what Richard Williams wrote about me in his blog: « If you’re ever at a loose end in Berlin on a Monday night, my advice would be to head for A-Trane, the jazz club in Charlottenburg, where Andreas Schmidt, a pianist, composer and teacher at the city’s Jazz Institut, holds a weekly free-admission session featuring a changing cast. Schmidt is a fine pianist, the salient features of his playing located somewhere between the Paul Bley of the mid-’60s and the Chick Corea of «Now He Sings, Now He Sobs». You might get an idea of his approach if I say that his first album was made (in 1995) with Lee Konitz, and a later one comprised a duo with Gary Peacock. His music is cerebral, but on the evidence I’ve heard it never lacks wit and humanity. » Richard Williams Andreas Schmidt, Piano

events.title: Oliver Koletzki – About the sun, the moon and the stars
Shuteen & Nils – «With Friends»
events.description: Shuteen & Nils with Friends FEAT : Roni Eytan-Luca Zambito-Sebastian Wolfgruber Deutsch Shuteen & Nils with Friends Zwei herausragende Stimmen des jungen europäischen Jazz – die mongolische Pianistin und Komponistin Shuteen Erdenebaatar und der deutsche Bassist und Klarinettist Nils Kugelmann – laden mit ihrem neuen Konzertformat „ Shuteen & Nils with Friends “ zu einer außergewöhnlichen musikalischen Reise ein. Das Programm vereint ausgewählte Stücke aus ihren gefeierten Konzertprogrammen Rising Sun, Bright Folk, Stormy Beauty und Life Score sowie aus ihrem Duo-Debüt Under the Same Stars. Die besondere musikalische Vielfalt entsteht nicht nur durch das Zusammenspiel ihrer Kompositionen, sondern auch durch die außergewöhnliche Besetzung: Shuteen Erdenebaatar am Klavier, Nils Kugelmann an der Kontraaltklarinette und am Bass, Roni Eytan an der Harmonika, Luca Zambito am Synthesizer und Sebastian Wolfgruber am Schlagzeug verschmelzen zu einem facettenreichen Ensembleklang. In der Musik von Shuteen und Nils treffen Jazz, Klassik und Filmmusik aufeinander. Die individuellen Geschichten, kulturellen Hintergründe und die gemeinsame Liebe zur Musik verweben sich zu einem eigenständigen musikalischen Dialog – voller überraschender Wendungen, klanglicher Vielfalt und emotionaler Tiefe. Shuteen Erdenebaatar und Nils Kugelmann haben sich in den vergangenen Jahren als prägende Persönlichkeiten einer neuen Generation des Jazz etabliert. Die in der Mongolei geborene Shuteen lebt seit 2018 in Deutschland und wurde unter anderem mit dem Deutschen Jazzpreis sowie dem höchsten Kulturpreis ihrer Heimat ausgezeichnet. Nils Kugelmann , ACT-Künstler und mehrfach preisgekrönter Musiker, ist sowohl mit seinem eigenen Trio als auch für seine unverwechselbare kompositorische Handschrift bekannt. Was mit einer persönlichen Begegnung begann, hat sich zu einem intensiven musikalischen Dialog entwickelt. Mit „Shuteen & Nils with Friends“ schlagen die beiden ein neues Kapitel auf und bringen ihre musikalischen Welten gemeinsam mit drei herausragenden Musikern in einer ebenso ungewöhnlichen wie inspirierenden Quintettbesetzung zusammen. English Shuteen & Nils with Friends Two outstanding voices of the new European jazz generation – Mongolian pianist and composer Shuteen Erdenebaatar and German bassist and clarinetist Nils Kugelmann – invite audiences on an extraordinary musical journey with their new concert project, “ Shuteen & Nils with Friends .” The programme brings together selected pieces from their acclaimed concert programmes Rising Sun, Bright Folk, Stormy Beauty and Life Score, alongside music from their duo debut album, Under the Same Stars . The project’s distinctive character lies not only in the interplay of their compositions but also in its unusual and colourful instrumentation. Shuteen Erdenebaatar on piano, Nils Kugelmann on contra-alto clarinet and bass, Roni Eytan on harmonica, Luca Zambito on synthesizer and Sebastian Wolfgruber on drums come together to create a rich and distinctive ensemble sound. The music of Shuteen and Nils brings jazz, classical music and film music into dialogue. Their individual stories, cultural backgrounds and shared love of music intertwine in a musical conversation full of unexpected turns, sonic diversity and emotional depth . In recent years, Shuteen Erdenebaatar and Nils Kugelmann have established themselves as defining figures of a new generation of jazz musicians. Born in Mongolia, Shuteen has been living in Germany since 2018 and has received numerous accolades, including the German Jazz Award and her homeland’s highest cultural honour. Nils Kugelmann , an ACT recording artist and multiple award-winning musician, is known both for his work with his own trio and for his distinctive compositional voice. What began as a personal encounter has grown into an intense musical dialogue. With “Shuteen & Nils with Friends“, the two artists open a new chapter, bringing their musical worlds together with three outstanding musicians in an unconventional and inspiring quintet setting . Shuteen Erdenebaatar – Piano, Composition Nils Kugelmann – Contra-Alto Clarinet, Double Bass, Composition Roni Eytan – Harmonica Luca Zambito – Synthesizer Sebastian Wolfgruber – Drums SHUTEEN & NILS Foto©Uli Neumann-Cosel Shuteen Erdenebaatar Foto©Dovile Sermokas NILS KUGELMANN Solo Foto©uli neumann-cosel Roni Eytan Foto©Adam Friedlander Luca Zambito Foto©Nils Kugelmann Sebastian Wolfgruber Foto©Daniel Nguyen

events.title: Life is Great
events.description:
Bad Angles Pt.I Release Show

The German/Danish quartet returns in the form of a super limited EP Cassette Mixtape featuring six songs you can only physically own in this exclusive format. Wuuut? Sounds crazy but it’s true.
There’s no better way to enjoy the nostalgic compositions of bandleader/drummer Johannes Koch. Along with Asger Nissen’s passionate sax-noodlin’, Thorbjørn Stefansson’s warm, experienced bass, Johannes “Jojo” Mann’s bright, shimmering guitar and just a little extra synth for that perfect retro twist.

This mixtape features 3 brand new tracks, a live version, a swanky demo, and even a phat remix from Regensburg producer Jellysquash. It’s jazz that’s best enjoyed from the comfort of your cabrio: for best results, drive with the top down, and volume way up.

LIFE IS GREAT: A Berlin based up-and-coming quartet lead by drummer/composer Johannes Koch, and consists of  Johannes “Jojo” Mann on guitar,  bassist Thorbjørn Stefansson, and saxophonist Asger Nissen.  Compositionally, Koch recreates the feeling of his teenage indie/postrock - years, navigating between naive simplicity, rhythmic complexity and energetic improvisation. With music like this - the kind that makes you stop for a moment and reflect, and maybe even smile - then just maybe, life is not so bad after all.

events.title: DJ Putilla
events.description:
Originally from Veracruz and based between Berlin and Mexico, DJ Putilla is a DJ, promoter, radio host, and founder of the itinerant queer party fiestuki, a project that connects Latinx talent and culture between Europe and Latin America.

Their work has been key in creating spaces and events that amplify the Latinx presence within Berlins electronic music scene, connecting rhythms, identities, and dialogues that transcend borders.

Their sound is reminiscent of the atmosphere of the port of Veracruz: hybrid sets that move between baile funk, bass, dembow, Latinx club, house, techno, and jungle, combining euphoria, darkness, and collective enjoyment.

They have performed in Mexico, Italy, Portugal, Poland, and Germany, including iconic Berlin clubs like OHM, Renate and Kater Blau, as well as festivals such as @bahidora and @mystic.creatures_. She is a resident of @refugeworldwide in Berlin and @pordetroit in Mexico City.

Jutta Speidel Seit mehr als 50 Jahren ist Jutta Speidel eine der beliebtesten Schauspielerinnen Deutschlands: im Film, im Fernsehen, auf der Bühne. Ihr Spiel ist genreübergreifend und umfasste und umfasst im Laufe der Jahre alles, was man spielen konnte und kann: junges Mädchen, Liebhaberin, Komödiantin, Nachdenkliche, Abenteuerin, Mörderin, Ehefrau, Verlassene, Mutter … Entdeckt wurde sie 1969 für die sogenannten ‚Pauker-Filme‘ aber schon 10 Jahre später begann ihre Theaterkarriere unter Rudolf Noelte in Berlin am Renaissance Theater. In den folgenden Jahren wechselten sich ihre beruflichen Engagements zwischen Film, Fernsehen und Theater ab. Sie spielte in Wien am Theater in der Josefstadt und am Burgtheater, an der Staatsoper München, im Festspielhaus Bad Hersfeld, in der Komödie im Bayerischen Hof, München und hatte zahlreiche Engagements in Stuttgart, Frankfurt, Karlsruhe und Düsseldorf sowie bei diversen Theatertourneen. So konnte sie einen breiten Publikum ihre Vielseitigkeit als Charakterschauspielerin zeigen. 1975 wurde der Filmregisseur Rainer Erler auf sie aufmerksam. Unter seiner Regie drehte sie u.a. den legendären Film ‘FLEISCH’, für den sie eine Filmpreisnominierung bekam. Im Laufe ihres Berufslebens folgten weit über 150 Filme, honoriert mit zahlreichen Preisen. Jutta Speidel gehört zu den erfolgreichsten Fernsehschauspielerinnen der letzten Jahre und sorgt mit ihrem Filmen immer wieder für höchste Einschaltquoten . Since 1995 I played here about 900 wonderful & surprising improvised happenings in music with lots of friends like Jay Clayton, Hayden Chisholm, Dave Douglas, Walter Norris, Mark Murphy, Till Brönner, Sebastian Merk, Andreas Edelmann, Jan Roder, Connie Crothers, Max Andrzejewski, Andy Fite etc.. events.title: ERNST BIER’S LITTLE SHOP OF JAZZ
events.description: CHRISTMAS SPECIAL ERNST BIER’S LITTLE SHOP OF JAZZ FEAT : CHRISTOPH ADAMS-PEPE BERNS Deutsch Diese drei Musiker kennen sich seit über 30 Jahren und haben schon in den verschiedensten Bands zusammengespielt. Kennen gelernt haben sie sich in den frühen 90‘ Jahren, als sie in Köln gelebt und musiziert haben. Der Pianist Christoph Adams spielte u.a. mit Ernst Bier und Ed Schuller im Trio und alle drei waren auch mehrere Jahre mit dem Klarinettisten Perry Robinson auf der Bühne zu hören. Davon gibt es mehrere CD-Veröffentlichungen. Der Bassist Pepe Berns war sowohl mit Christoph Adams als auch mit Ernst Bier in zahlreichen Projekten aktiv und europaweit auf Tour. Die drei Musiker leben und arbeiten in Berlin. Lassen Sie sich mitreißen von der ungeheuren Spiellaune dieser exzellenten Musiker. Sie leben mit und durch ihre Musik, eine Tatsache, die sie ausnahmslos an die Zuhörer weitergeben . English These three musicians have known each other for over 30 years and have played together in a wide variety of bands. They met in the early ’90s, when they were living and performing in Cologne. Pianist Christoph Adams played in a trio with Ernst Bier and Ed Schuller, among others, and all three also performed on stage with clarinetist Perry Robinson for several years. Several CDs have been released documenting these performances. Bassist Pepe Berns has been active in numerous projects with both Christoph Adams and Ernst Bier and has toured throughout Europe. The three musicians live and work in Berlin. Let yourself be swept away by the incredible enthusiasm of these excellent musicians. They live with and through their music—a passion they unquestionably share with their audience . Christoph Adams – Piano Pepe Berns – Bass Ernst Bier – Drums

events.title: ERNST BIER NEW TRIO – «TRIPLE»
events.description: ERNST BIER NEW TRIO « TRIPLE » FEAT : Tal Arditi-Christian Müller Deutsch Triple ist ein neues Bandprojekt vom Schlagzeuger Ernst Bier . Im Februar spielten der Gitarrist Tal Arditi , der Bassist Christian Müller und Schlagzeuger Ernst Bier zum ersten Mal im Jazzclub A-Trane miteinander. Die Chemie zwischen den Musikern stimmte sofort und das Publikum war begeistert. Das veranlasste die Musiker dazu ein neues Trio zu gründen und hier sind sie noch einmal „ back by popular demand “! Lassen Sie sich mitreißen von der ungeheuren Spiellaune dieser exzellenten Musiker. Sie leben mit und durch ihre Musik, eine Tatsache, die sie ausnahmslos mit viel Freude an die Zuhörer weitergeben . Tal Arditi ist ein israelischer, in Berlin lebender Jazz-Gitarrist und Komponist. Anerkannt als junges Gitarrenwunder, begann Tal im Alter von 16 Jahren mit dem Studium im prestigeträchtigen „Jazzinstitut“ – Programm der „Rimon Music University“. Im Alter von 18 Jahren schloss er auf der renommierten Rimon School of Music in Ramat Hasharon in der Nähe von Tel Aviv erfolgreich mit einem Jazz-Diplom ab und beschloss nach Berlin zu ziehen. In Berlin wurde Tal Arditi schnell zu einem der gefragtesten Musiker in der internationalen und lokalen Jazzszene und begann, regelmäßig in Clubs in ganz Europa sowie auf Festivals wie dem Umbria Jazz-Festival, dem Xjazz Festival, dem Red Sea Festival, dem Fusion Festival oder dem Open Air Keintal zu spielen. Christian Müller ist Bassist und Komponist, der nach den Stationen Hamburg und Amsterdam, seit 2019 den Mittelpunkt seines Schaffens nach Berlin verlegt hat. Er studierte an der HfMT Hamburg sowie am Conservatorium van Amsterdam. Parallel dazu wurde er ins Bundesjazzorchester (BujazzO) unter der Leitung von Niels Klein und Jiggs Whigham aufgenommen. Konzertreisen führten ihn auf Bühnen in- und außerhalb Deutschlands. Unter anderem: Elbjazz-Festival (DE), Jazz Baltica-Festival(DE), Jazzkaar Festival (EST), Borneo Jazz Festival (MYS). In der Vergangenheit spielte er mit: John Schröder, Tony Malaby, Gilad Hekselmanm Seamus Blake, Marcio Doctor, Wanja Slavin, Ensemble Resonanz und noch vielen weiteren fabelhaften Musikerinnen. Christians Arbeit als Sideman ist auf mehreren Alben mit diversen Projekten dokumentiert. Ende 2025 kam sein Debütalbum „Golden Gloom“ heraus, welches ausschließlich Eigenkompositionen enthält. Ernst Bier studierte Schlagzeug bei Billy Brooks, Charlie Persip, Vernell Fournier und Elvin Jones. Von 1983-1987 lebte und arbeitete er in NY-City. Nach seiner Rückkehr aus den Staaten lebte Ernst zunächst bei Köln und dann ab 1992 in Berlin. Die Liste der Musiker, mit denen er gearbeitet hat, liest sich wie ein Who’s Who des Jazz. Mit seinem einfühlsamen Spiel, seiner Hingabe und seiner konstruktiven Art hat er sich zu einem hochgeschätzten und gefragten Schlagzeuger entwickelt. English Triple is a new band project by drummer Ernst Bier . In February, guitarist Tal Arditi , bassist Christian Müller , and drummer Ernst Bier played together for the first time at the A-Trane Jazz Club. The chemistry between the musicians clicked immediately, and the audience was thrilled. This inspired the musicians to form a new trio, and here they are once again “ back by popular demand ”! Let yourself be swept away by the incredible enthusiasm of these excellent musicians. They live with and through their music—a passion they consistently share with their audience with great joy . Tal Arditi is an Israeli jazz guitarist and composer living in Berlin. Recognized as a young guitar prodigy, Tal began studying at the prestigious “Jazz Institute” program at Rimon Music University at the age of 16. At the age of 18, he successfully graduated with a jazz diploma from the renowned Rimon School of Music in Ramat Hasharon near Tel Aviv and decided to move to Berlin. In Berlin, Tal Arditi quickly became one of the most sought-after musicians on the international and local jazz scene and began playing regularly in clubs throughout Europe as well as at festivals such as the Umbria Jazz Festival, the Xjazz Festival, the Red Sea Festival, the Fusion Festival, and the Open Air Keintal. Christian Müller is a bassist and composer who, after spending time in Hamburg and Amsterdam, moved his creative center to Berlin in 2019. He studied at the HfMT Hamburg and the Conservatorium van Amsterdam. At the same time, he was accepted into the Bundesjazzorchester (BujazzO) under the direction of Niels Klein and Jiggs Whigham. Concert tours have taken him to stages in Germany and abroad. Among others: Elbjazz Festival (DE), Jazz Baltica Festival (DE), Jazzkaar Festival (EST), Borneo Jazz Festival (MYS). In the past, he has played with John Schröder, Tony Malaby, Gilad Hekselman, Seamus Blake, Marcio Doctor, Wanja Slavin, Ensemble Resonanz, and many other fabulous musicians. Christian’s work as a sideman is documented on several albums with various projects. At the end of 2025, his debut album “Golden Gloom” was released, which contains exclusively his own compositions. Ernst Bier studied percussion with Billy Brooks, Charlie Persip, Vernell Fournier, and Elvin Jones. From 1983 to 1987, he lived and worked in New York City. After returning from the United States, Ernst first lived near Cologne and then, from 1992, in Berlin. The list of musicians he has worked with reads like a who’s who of jazz. With his sensitive playing, dedication, and constructive approach, he has become a highly regarded and sought-after drummer. Tal Arditi – Guitar Christian Müller – Bass Ernst Bier – Drums
